Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update – Pivotal Phase 3 ENSURE-1 and ENSURE-2 Trials of Vidofludimus Calcium in Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis Remain on Track, with Top-Line Data Expected in December 2026 – – Initiation of Phase 3 PROTECT-MS Trial of Vidofludimus Calcium in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis Ongoing, with First-Patient-Enrolled Expected in the First Half of 2027 – – Executive Leadership Team Further Strengthened with Appointments of Chief Data and Digital Officer and Chief People Officer to Support Regulatory and Commercial Readiness – NEW YORK, November 13, 2026 – Immunic, Inc.

“As we approach the top-line data from our Phase 3 ENSURE trials in relapsing multiple sclerosis (MS) in December, we believe Immunic is entering one of the most important periods in its history,” said Erik Lundgren, Chief Executive Officer of Immunic.
“Further, our Phase 3 ENSURE trials in relapsing MS continue to be on track to report top-line data in December 2026.
Our teams remain focused on this readout and readiness for a potential NDA submission should the results be positive.

Anticipated Clinical Milestones ● Vidofludimus Calcium in Relapsing MS: Top-line data from the twin Phase 3 ENSURE-1 and ENSURE-2 trials remains on track and is expected to be available in December 2026.

If positive, Immunic plans to submit an NDA in the United States in mid-2027, with a targeted potential regulatory approval date in 2028. ● Vidofludimus Calcium in Progressive MS: The initiation of the Phase 3 PROTECT-MS trial in progressive MS is ongoing, with first-patient-enrolled expected in the first half of 2027. ● IMU-381: The IMU-381 program, selected to leverage the Nurr1 platform for neurologic and autoimmune diseases, continues to be in preclinical testing with lead candidate identification ongoing.

The company’s lead investigational asset , vidofludimus calcium (IMU-838), is currently being evaluated in Phase 3 clinical trials in relapsing multiple sclerosis, with top-line data expected to be available in December 2026.
